name: George Francis Adams Sr.
personality: Did not bring his work home
Prioritized his wife Beryl above all else
The most important thing in his life was my Mom
notable_stories: A professional military law enforcement officer (Provost Marshall) who did not bring his work home and prioritized his wife, Beryl, above all else
Drafted for WWII: MP, self-defense instructor, Commander of POW camp holding Japanese combatants in Hawaii
Recalled for Korean War: Commander of MP detachment in Okinawa

Postings: Presidio SF (1954), Ft. Gordon GA, Frankfurt/Heidelberg (1958–62), Presidio SF (1962–), South Korea (13 months unaccompanied), retired as Provost Marshall of Ft. Lewis / Eastern Washington (1971)
1930 census listed as George F. Wells, step-son — Arthur Wells was his step-father
Arthur died when John was in 11th grade (~1963-64); Nini then moved in with John's family in San Francisco until her own death in 1967
Prior career included Union Oil / Standard Oil truck driver and St. Martin's College Olympia
Recorded correctly as step-child with surname Adams on the 1930 census (not Wells)
Cause of death confirmed: cancer, 'probably self-inflicted' — he was a moderate smoker and daily drinker (John's memoir).
He was a 'prototypical, Greatest Generation Soldier.'
Drafted first for WWII, then recalled for the Korean Conflict. After that he decided to make the Army his career.
WWII: served in Hawaii as a Military Police Officer, self-defense instructor, and Commander of a POW camp holding Japanese combatants.
Korean Conflict: Commander of the Military Police detachment in Okinawa.
First Presidio SF assignment (1954): attended San Francisco State University and finished his college degree; in charge of the stockade.
Germany (1958-62): in charge of the Military Police who rode the German trains.
Back at Presidio SF (1962): administrative job as coordinator of industrial defense on the west coast.
South Korea: assigned Provost Marshall of South Korea, went unaccompanied for 13 months.
Final assignment: Provost Marshall of Ft. Lewis and Eastern Washington, retired 1971.
Started taking family movies in Okinawa, sporadically continued through John's high school years.
At one point he told John: 'Don't expect praise. If they aren't dumping on you, you are doing just fine.'

The 1930 census taker wrongly recorded him as George F. Wells, though his relationship to the head of household was correctly given as stepson. His siblings Presley and Edith were correctly listed as stepchildren surnamed Adams.
A family photo of George and Serena shows their son (George Sr.) at about 3 years old, taken shortly before his father's death in 1920.
milestones: Married Beryl Simons Adams (m. 2 Jul 1942, Franklin County, WA)
Worked for Union Oil before being recalled for the Korean Conflict
Served as an MP officer in Okinawa, Germany, and the U.S.
Married Beryl Eva Simons (2 July 1942, Franklin County, WA)
Retired from U.S. Army 1971 as Provost Marshall of Ft. Lewis / Eastern Washington
Military police officer at the Presidio, San Francisco, where the family lived while John and George Jr. grew up
Census 1940: San Francisco, California, aged 24, single, stepson of Arthur T. Wells; living in Burlingame, San Mateo County, in 1935
sources: Descendants of Jose Pierre Adams, compiled by William W. "Bill" Allen (2 April 2011 edition)
Newspaper clippings and obituaries in Bill Allen’s family document (2011)
Family research emails, 2011–2013 (John and Barbara Adams with Irma Kulp Zacher, George F. Adams, Bill Allen and others)
1940 U.S. census, Assembly District 22, San Francisco, California, ED 38-131, sheet 12B (FamilySearch index, accessed 2 Apr 2013)
notes: Referenced in Brendan McKeldin Adams: Paternal grandparents are Beryl Adams and George Francis Adams II
Also referred to as George Francis Adams Sr. Siblings listed: Presley Marcason, Edith V.
Marriage to Beryl Eva Simons: 2 July 1942, Franklin County, WA — confirmed.
Rosemary Wells was his step-sister (Arthur Wells' biological daughter, ~1916), raised essentially as his sister. Prior source had birth listed as 10 Mar 1916 — confirmed here.
Cause of death: cancer, moderate smoker and daily drinker (John's memoir). Confirms 1980 death.

CORRECTION 2026-09-22: Removed a block of family-wide places (Posen, Battle Creek, Honolulu, Tacoma …) that had been copied onto 48 records; kept only those that belong to this person: San Francisco, CA.
Pictured as 'George Jr.' in a c. 1919 family photograph with George F., Serena, Edith and Presley [Bill Allen, Descendants of Jose Pierre Adams, 2011, line 6079]
As George Adams, he appears in a census in the household of his stepfather Arthur T. Wells, after his father's death. [Family research emails, email 17]

He was always known as 'Sr.' rather than III; his son George writes that technically he was George II, because of a generation gap between the first two George Francis Adamses. [Family research emails, email 31]
Unconfirmed: His mother Neenie seems to have changed his name from Edward G. to George F. some time after his father died. [Family research emails, email 17]
Unconfirmed: His sister Trudy said he was 2 years old when his father died in 1918, a date the brothers later doubted. [Family research emails, email 30]
Unconfirmed: His son George can only guess that the 'G' in Edward G. stood for George. [Family research emails, email 31]

Open question: George Francis Adams Sr. appears as Edward G. in the 1920 census, and Oregon birth certificates exist under both names. Did Neenie rename him after his father died? What did the 'G' stand for (guessed George)? John asks 'where did Edward come from?' [Family research emails, email 17, 31]

The 1920 census of his parents' household in Douglas County, Oregon, lists a son "Edward G. Adams", aged 3 years 9 months (born about 1916-17, Oregon), and no other young son; George, born 10 Mar 1916, would have been 3 years 10 months. The emails say Oregon birth certificates exist under both names. Brendan Adams doubts they are the same person; left open. [1920 U.S. census, Douglas County, Oregon, household 51, sheet 9 (FamilySearch index, accessed 2 Apr 2013)]
